highlights.title: Your car’s data privacy problems are worse than you think
highlights.summary: You hear it all the time: Modern cars are basically smartphones on wheels. And just like the phone in your pocket, the car in your driveway collects vast amounts of data - tracking where you drive, how fast you accelerate, how hard you brake, how aggressively you turn, and much more.
body: A team of researchers tested 21 vehicles and found that all of them transmitted data to a third-party domain. And over half were pinging advertising companies.

This week, researchers from Northeastern University, in collaboration with Consumer Reports, published an in-depth examination of connected vehicle privacy behaviors. Utilizing nearly two dozen vehicles from CR ’s test fleet, the team sought to answer critical questions: Which cars transmit data? Who receives it? Does it cross international borders? And what personally identifiable information is actually being exposed?

David Choffnes, project lead and former director of Northeastern’s Cybersecurity and Privacy Institute, said the goal was to reveal the sheer scale of modern vehicle data tracking and highlight how little visibility or control owners truly have over it.
“I think the conclusion is that there’s a lot to be worried about,” Choffnes said in an interview.

highlights.title: The effects of an “algorithmic monoculture” depend on the details
highlights.summary: In a study focusing on hiring decisions, MIT researchers found the use of a single algorithm by many firms could benefit job seekers in certain situations.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."

AI tools are increasingly replacing human judgements in some settings. For instance, resume screening algorithms are often used in hiring, where they may improve efficiency and consistency in decision-making.

But some scholars have raised concerns that the adoption of automated systems could eventually result in one algorithm being used to make all decisions in a particular industry. They worry so-called algorithmic monoculture could have negative consequences.

For example, in hiring, the thinking goes that algorithmic monoculture might result in systematic exclusion — a situation in which a job candidate rejected by one firm’s algorithm would likely also be rejected by every other firm’s algorithm.

highlights.title: Keenum rolls back years to lead Chicago Bears to win over Philadelphia Eagles
highlights.summary: Case Keenum passed for two touchdowns in his first NFL start in almost three years as Chicago Bears shut down Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles for a 27-7 victory on Monday night.
body: Stepping in for Caleb Williams, Keenum starred completing 24 passes from 34 attempts to make 247 yards. He also scored his first rushing touchdown since 2019 on a one-yard plunge with seven minutes and 19 seconds left to play, capping a 13-play drive that took more than eight minutes off the clock.
It was Keenum's first action since he started for Houston in a 36-22 loss to Cleveland in December 2023.
"To get a shot again like this? You dream of it," Keenum said. "That's why I'm still here doing this when I get knocked down.
"I got knocked down my whole career. I just keep getting up, coming to work, just keep bouncing back."

highlights.title: Houseplant hacks: should you water plants less in winter?
highlights.summary: Don’t water based on the month or the season – be led by what the plant is actually doing. The problem Cutting back on watering for winter has become so ingrained that people start rationing by the calendar, giving plants just a fraction of the water they had in summer, because the season changed.
body: The hack The advice to reduce is because, as light levels drop, most houseplants slow their growth, use less water and dry out more slowly, so watering as you did in summer risks waterlogging the roots and causing rot.
The method When we get to October, reduce watering to half or a quarter of what you gave plants in the summer.

The test I reduced watering in two of my own plants last winter. A calathea in a cooler, dimmer room dried out more slowly and needed less watering, exactly as the hack predicts. But a pothos sitting under a grow light in a warm room kept growing and started crisping at the edges and dropping yellow leaves.

The verdict The winter watering rule is not a myth, but it is badly misunderstood. The key is to water according to what the plant is doing, not what the calendar says. Research your plant to see if it has a dormant season and check each plant before you water. Push a finger a couple of inches into the compost, or lift the pot to feel its weight – a bone-dry pot is light, a wet one is heavy.
points: Don’t water based on the month or the season – be led by what the plant is actually doing.

highlights.title: Beats 360 Review: Customizable, Stylish, and Fun
highlights.summary: Beats’ new flagship headphones are customizable, stylish, fun, and great for working out. But there are stronger options for everyday use.
body: The Beats 360, I'll admit, didn't click for me until I started thinking of them as over-ear workout headphones. As everyday headphones, I had a tough time ranking these, given the competition, but as gym cans, the Beats 360 are stellar.

It took me a while to come to this conclusion because working out with over-ear headphones has always kind of sucked. They shift around a lot, get warm and sweaty around your ears, and are way, way heavier than earbuds. That last part might not seem like a big deal, but if you’re running a half-marathon, a half-pound weight on top of your head starts to get annoying fast. This stigma made me ignore this attribute about the Beats 360 at first.

Still, the number of people I see working out (and running) with Apple AirPods Max, one of the heaviest popular over-ear headphones around, shows the demand is there. And the Beats 360 fulfill that niche brilliantly, with a secure fit, IPX4-rated water resistance, and swappable cushioning. They may not be the best over-ear headphones for other things (like high-resolution audio), but it’s hard to knock them when they get their main thing (customizable over-ear workout headphones) right.

highlights.title: Who we become when we talk to machines
highlights.summary: Professor Sherry Turkle’s new book, “Artificial Intimacy,” offers a withering critique of chatbots and the antisocial dynamics she believes they encourage.
body: Brian, a middle-aged financial consultant, spends his day sitting in front of three screens. Two of them involve his job. The third features a chatbot, which he has given a woman’s name and frequently uses. Brian spent years on the road for work earlier in his career, has never married, and recently broke up with a woman who said he was emotionally unavailable. What did Brian do, in response? He asked the chatbot if the woman had a point.

“It’s an extraordinary moment,” writes MIT Professor Sherry Turkle, who interviewed Brian (not his real name) while conducting her research for her new book about chatbots. “Brian asks an object with no emotions to tell him if he is emotionally withholding: ‘Speak to me about what you cannot experience.’ As soon as he asks the program to talk about intimacy, he’s asking it to punch above its weight.”
And yet, this kind of thing seems to be happening a lot today.

highlights.summary: X-Men star Alan Cumming has admitted he "didn't fully understand" the plot of Avengers: Doomsday while filming his scenes — one of which involved getting close to Florence Pugh's Black Widow.
body: If this latest tidbit from the Traitors host sounds familiar, it's because Cumming has leaked snippets about his time on Marvel's set previously — lamenting that his returning character Nightcrawler was filmed mostly against blue screen, and noting that he had got to fight Pedro Pascal's Reed Richards.

Now, Cumming has told SiriusXM (via Variety ) that he did have bits of Doomsday's story explained to him — only for him to respond that he didn't really need to know the plot as he was simply there to "run around."
Cumming also revealed that he had to, at one point, lie on top of Florence Pugh's Black Widow character — even though it was her stunt double that he actually laid upon.

"There was a bit when we were shooting a scene, and it was one of the rare scenes when I was actually on the backlot and not in front of a blue screen," Cumming began. "And this man came and said, 'So right now Alan, these giant robots are blah blah,' and started to tell me the thing, and I was like, 'You know what, thank you so much, but just tell me where I point my, whatever I point. And I'll do that. Really, I just know I'm here to run around'."

highlights.title: Trial of live facial recognition cameras in London stations ends with one false positive
highlights.summary: Freedom of information request shows six-month trial cost £320,000, used almost 100 police hours and resulted in no arrests. A six-month trial of live facial recognition (LFR) technology in London’s railway stations that cost more than £320,000 and almost 100 hours of police officers’ time ended in…
body: More than half a million faces were scanned between February and July this year in some of the capital’s busiest transport hubs during the British Transport Police (BTP) trial of the surveillance technology, which aimed to help catch offenders and people breaching court orders.

A freedom of information document obtained by Liberty Investigates and shared with the Guardian shows that equipment hire and police staffing for the 18 deployments across the trial cost the taxpayer £320,786 and led to only one alert on a watchlist, which turned out to be an incorrect identification, also known as a false positive.
Last month BTP announced it was extending the trial for a further four months and expanding the deployments to include London Underground stations.

When Transport for London announced its support for the extension of the trial, it said LFR technology “will target and identify people on police watchlists at key stations chosen for maximum impact” and would “specifically tackle violence against women and girls, whose travel behaviours are shaped by experiences of sexual harassment and sexual offences”.

highlights.title: American exodus: why do so many US NHL stars want out of Canada?
highlights.summary: Players across the league are leaving their teams up north to return home. It’s prompted questions around money, tax rates, geopolitics and respect. Back in September 1925, Frederick Wilson, sports editor at the Globe, explained the fear among hockey fans that Canadian teams might not be able to…
body: At the time, Wilson reassured everyone that, no matter the big US cash, everyone on the ice would be Canadian anyway. “It will be some years before the [US] will be in a position to furnish players,” he wrote. He was right about that. It took a long time for the US to catch up to Canada in on-ice talent. But now that it has, should we expect Americans to want to play anywhere else than the US? For 100 years Canada has worried that the US would just buy all the best hockey players. But now it makes its own and, as the new NHL season gets underway on Tuesday night, they want to go home.

It’s difficult to pinpoint where this all started. But the general feeling, given the timing, is that something happened around this year’s Olympics that prompted US-born players to turn their backs on Canada. Maybe it started earlier, in 2025, after the 4 Nations Face-Off. Or maybe it was just in the wind, given the new geopolitical tensions between the two countries. In any event, as the 2026-27 NHL season kicks off Tuesday, the divide is back – or at least seems to have deepened.

highlights.title: Plastic Is Melting Onto Corals
highlights.summary: Scientists have found a new form of pollution, one where plastic and pieces of coral become irreversibly intertwined.
body: Marine plastic pollution is rampant. That’s nothing new. Plastic waste has been found in a variety of marine ecosystems, including beaches, coral reefs, and even some of the ocean’s farthest depths. While a precise measurement is difficult, it’s estimated that several million metric tons of plastic lie on the seafloor.

Scientists have been recording marine animals entangled in or consuming plastic debris for over half a century, some even proposing the term “Plastocene” (the Plastic Age) to denote the geological epoch spanning from the 1950s onward. And now researchers have discovered a new way these substances are polluting the environment: Plastic is fusing with corals.

The discovery of this conglomerate—which researchers have dubbed “plasticoral”—was made during a survey of the beaches of the Ryukyu Islands in southern Japan. The scientists noticed small, brightly colored spots embedded in the white coral gravel. They collected samples from three beaches on the main island, Okinawa, and brought them to the lab where spectroscopic analysis revealed there were polymers derived from common household plastics.

body: The deal is expected to close by the end of the year. Li will become EVP and chief scientist at AMD, reporting to AMD CEO Lisa Su, while the World Labs team will “continue to focus on advancing AI model research.” AMD also notes that the acquisition will strengthen “its ability to develop AI hardware, software and systems around the needs of emerging models and applications.”

“Just like I knew it was time to do a startup to jumpstart the work of creating foundation models beyond LLMs and achieve the most impact in AI, it’s again very clear that the right path for myself and World Labs is to continue our mission as a part of AMD,” Li says in a post on her Substack. “Together we’re committed to keep pushing the frontier of AI to solve real problems, and doing so openly with the community and the entire ecosystem.”

A potential merger between the BBC and Channel 4, which would be a monumental shakeup in the U.K. TV industry, has been mooted before. Back in 2024, reports emerged that the idea was being discussed, a move that at the was claimed would add more than $1.3 billion to the BBC’s coffers and enable Channel 4’s to cut costs, free up budget to be spent on commissioning new programmes and use its profits to subsidise other parts of the BBC.

According to The Guardian, another reported model was for Channel 4 — which several years ago was under threat of privatisation by the then Conservative government — to operate as a semi-independent entity under BBC Studios, the BBC’s for-profit arm.
At the time, a BBC spokesperson said there were “no ongoing discussions” about the merger of the BBC and Channel 4 “nor are we developing a proposal to do so.”

The couple inside aren’t missing theirs: they’re taking endless selfies in the clinical pink-and-turquoise carriage that looks like a hospital canteen and smells like cinnamon buns and strong filter coffee.

I’m on Snälltåget’s iconic red-shelled train, on the Swedish rail company’s new route from Malmö to Oslo – a 6.5-hour journey along Sweden’s picturesque western corridor. Until now, the journey between the two cities involved long bus rides and fragmented train transfers. This direct line is easier and cheaper, with tickets starting at £11 each way. It’s already a hit, shuttling more than 25,000 passengers since launching this summer.

I was first seduced by Scandi rail travel a decade ago on a journey from Stockholm to Gothenburg, when I was berthed in a cosy dark-wood cabin and listened to a pianist play in a dining car. This time, starting in Malmö, I will take advantage of the new route to make a series of stops along the country’s western shore.

highlights.summary: OpenAI apologises for incidents involving Australian government websites and outlines stronger safeguards and support to strengthen Australia’s cyber defences.
body: In June, during internal training and evaluation our models accessed Australian government websites in ways they were not authorised to. We also should have handled our response better. We are sorry and working to do better in the future.

In this post, we are setting out what we know, what we have changed, and what we will do to rebuild trust with the Australian people. This is a new kind of cyber incident which represents an emerging global challenge. One of the ways we intend to take accountability for the situation is to be intentional in working with Australia to help develop practical approaches to how AI developers and governments identify, disclose, and respond to AI cyber behaviour, whether malicious or unintentional.

After the Hugging Face incident in July, we began reviewing earlier training and evaluation activity to identify other affected organisations. In mid-August, that review identified activity affecting the Australian government websites below.

highlights.title: The pest I’ll never forget: I turned the toaster upside down. A mouse fell out
highlights.summary: We tried humane traps, wire wool, hardcore cleaning regimes. Nothing worked. In the end, I wondered if the mice in our house were the real residents, while we were the intruders. Some of the happiest years of my 20s were spent in a house-share in east London.
body: We were also not particularly clean, which meant our cluttered, chaotic house was the ideal home for mice. At first we told ourselves it was just one mouse we saw running along next to the skirting board or darting behind a sofa. But a quick scan of the internet confirmed our fears that it’s never just one – mice are social creatures, and they were likely in a nest-share similar to our house-share. A female mouse gives birth to a litter of five to eight mice and can be pregnant up to 10 times a year. We read forum posts that claimed mice were doubly incontinent (something I’ve since learned is fake news), and our horror began to grow.

As the sightings increased and droppings appeared on the kitchen worktop, we agreed something had to be done. Two of my housemates were vegetarian, so we laid humane traps, with a plan to set the creatures free in the garden or a park. The humane traps did not work. The mice continued to thrive and multiply.
points: We tried humane traps, wire wool, hardcore cleaning regimes.
In the end, I wondered if the mice in our house were the real residents, while we were the intruders.

videos.title: Eagles score TD as Jalen Hurts snaps ball with a second left in half | NFL on ESPN
videos.summary: After DeVonta Smith is tackled short of the goal line, the Eagles hurry up and snap the ball with a second left, allowing Jalen Hurts to punch it in for a touchdown that cuts the Bears’ lead to 10-7 at halftime of Monday Night Football.
